Description: First-time setup flow where a new user configures their account (name, username, profile details, initial preferences) right after signing up.
Onboarding walkthrough, product tour, or step-by-step tutorial that explains features to a first-time user, often with coach marks, highlighted regions, or progress dots.
Account creation screen with fields like email, password, name, or social sign-up buttons (Continue with Google/Apple).
Screens for verifying identity via email code, SMS OTP, phone number confirmation, CAPTCHA, or two-factor authentication challenge.
Screens that let a user permanently delete or temporarily deactivate their account, usually with warnings and a final confirmation.
Password recovery flow: enter email, receive a reset link/code, and set a new password.
Sign-in screen with email/username and password fields, biometric prompt, or SSO buttons.
User-owned profile or account overview showing personal info, avatar, username, stats, and editable fields.
App-wide settings hub: account, notifications, privacy, appearance, language, accessibility, and similar toggles organized in a list.
Success or completion screen confirming an action was performed (e.g., 'Payment complete', 'Message sent'), often with a large checkmark or celebratory illustration.
Screen or sheet offering the user a set of choices before continuing, such as action sheets, option pickers, or 'What do you want to do?' menus.
A 'Are you sure?' screen or modal asking the user to confirm a destructive or important action before it is executed.
Screen shown when there is no content to display yet (empty inbox, no search results, no items), usually with an illustration and a call to action.
Error screen or message indicating something went wrong (failed request, 404, crash, form validation summary) with an explanation and recovery option.
Informational screen describing a feature, often shown when it launches or is first opened, including 'What's new' and feature highlight screens.
Screens asking the user for feedback: rating the app, leaving a comment, NPS survey, or a 'How was your experience?' prompt.
Help center, FAQ, contact support, chat-with-us, or troubleshooting screens.
A screen dominated by a loading indicator, spinner, progress bar, or skeleton placeholders while content is being fetched.
Screens or system prompts requesting permissions (notifications, camera, microphone, location, contacts, Bluetooth).
Screen that recommends content to the user: 'You may also like', 'Recommended for you', related items, or personalized suggestions.
Billing and invoicing screens showing charges, invoices, receipts, or billing history for a subscription or account.
Shopping cart or bag screen listing items the user has added, with quantities, price totals, and a checkout button.
Multi-step checkout flow: shipping address, delivery option, payment, and review-and-pay screens.
Post-purchase confirmation screen showing 'Thanks for your order', order number, summary, and estimated delivery.
Detail view for a single order showing items purchased, status, tracking, shipping address, and totals.
List of the user's past orders or purchases, each with status and a link to details.
Screens for adding, editing, or selecting a payment method (credit card, PayPal, Apple Pay, bank account).
Plan comparison or pricing tier screens showing feature-by-feature comparisons and prices.
Screens showcasing coupons, promo codes, loyalty rewards, referral bonuses, or seasonal discounts.
Storefront landing or browse screen showing products, categories, featured collections, or a branded shop.
Upgrade, subscription, or paywall screens presenting plan options and a 'Subscribe' / 'Upgrade' call to action.
Wallet overview showing account balance, points, credits, cards, or cryptocurrency holdings.
Screens showing badges, trophies, streaks, or milestone awards earned by the user.
Conversation view inside a messaging app showing a thread of messages with one contact or group.
Comment thread on a post, article, video, or product showing replies, likes, and reply composer.
List of users someone follows or is followed by, with follow/unfollow buttons.
Screens to invite people by email, link, or contact list to a team, workspace, or group.
Ranked list of users or teams by score, points, or activity, usually with position, avatar, and metric.
Notifications inbox listing alerts, activity, mentions, and system messages with unread indicators.
Screens showing star ratings, reviews, or a form to leave a review for a product, place, or service.
Chronological or algorithmic feed of posts from followed users, including likes, comments, and share actions.
Profile page for another user or a group/community, showing avatar, bio, stats, and their content.
Long-form article or blog post reading view with title, byline, body text, and inline images.
Browse, explore, or discover screens with categories, curated sections, or search-driven discovery.
Detail screen for an online course, class, or lesson with description, chapters, and 'Start' or 'Resume' actions.
Screens showing a code editor, IDE, or code playground with syntax-highlighted code and file tree.
Email inbox, message list, or email reading view (not 1-on-1 chat — think Gmail-style mail).
Detail view for an event: title, date/time, location, description, attendees, and RSVP button.
Detail view for a goal, task, to-do, ticket, or project item with assignee, status, and description.
Primary landing or home screen of an app — the dashboard the user sees first after launch or login.
News or article feed with headlines, thumbnails, and summaries (distinct from a social feed of user posts).
A single note or document view in a notes/notebook app with rich text, attachments, or markdown.
Catch-all for content detail screens that don't fit the other Content categories.
Detail view for a social post showing the full post, media, author, likes, and comments.
Product detail page: images, title, price, description, variants, reviews, and 'Add to cart' button.
Quiz, test, or question-and-answer screens with multiple-choice options, progress, and scoring.
Detail view for a cooking recipe: ingredients, instructions, cook time, and hero photo.
Now-playing or detail screen for a song, album, or podcast episode with artwork and playback controls.
Full-screen, tap-to-advance story viewer (Instagram/Snapchat-style) with progress bars at the top.
Detail page for a movie or show with poster, synopsis, cast, ratings, and a 'Play' button.
Screens for creating something new: new post, new project, new file, 'Create' flows and forms.
Screens to block, mute, or ban a user, with warnings or reason selectors.
Screens to cancel a subscription, order, booking, or in-progress action.
Screens focused on deleting an item, with a confirmation and usually a destructive red button.
Drawing, sketching, markup, or annotation canvases with pen, brush, and shape tools.
Edit mode for an existing item (post, profile, document) with editable fields and Save/Cancel.
Screens about favoriting, pinning, or starring items, or lists of the user's favorites.
Filter and sort panels or sheets with multi-select options, ranges, and an 'Apply' button.
Screens to report content or a user, usually with reason options and a text box.
Screens to follow a user, channel, or topic, or subscribe to a feed, newsletter, or channel.
Screens to import data from other services or export data to a file or another service.
Referral screens: share invite link, earn rewards for invites, and track pending invites.
Screens centered on liking, upvoting, or reacting to content with counts and reaction pickers.
Screens to move an item to a different folder, list, board, or category.
Catch-all for action-focused screens that don't fit the other Action categories.
Publish, post, or send flow: finalize content and push it live, often with visibility and scheduling options.
Screens or modes for reordering items in a list via drag handles or up/down controls.
Screens focused on saving something — save-to-collection, save as draft, or save-changes dialogs.
Scheduling screens: pick a date/time to post, send, book, or run something in the future.
Search entry screens, live search results, suggestions, and recent-search lists.
Multi-select or item-picker modes where the user taps to select one or many items, often with a bulk-action bar.
Screens for setting a value or configuration — alarms, reminders, goals, temperatures, thresholds.
Share sheets, share-to-social screens, and link-sharing screens with copy/share options.
Money-movement screens: send, transfer, request, or receive funds, with amount, recipient, and confirmation.
Screens for uploading files or media, and screens showing download progress or managing downloads.
Screens where charts or graphs (line, bar, pie, area) are the primary content, often with filters and legends.
Analytics dashboard: KPI tiles, charts, and data summaries on one screen, often customizable.
Progress tracking screens: habit streaks, fitness progress, goal completion, XP bars, and milestones.
User-saved items organized into folders, collections, or boards (saved posts, bookmarked articles, wishlists).
Playlist screens for music, video, or podcasts showing ordered tracks and playback controls.
Trash, recycle bin, or archive screens where deleted or archived items can be restored or purged.
Dedicated audio playback screen with artwork, scrubber, play/pause, next/previous, and volume.
Recording screens for voice memos or video with a record button, waveform or viewfinder, and timer.
Calendar views: month, week, day, or agenda with events on a grid or timeline.
Voice or video call screens: incoming call, in-call UI with mute/hangup, and call history.
Infinite or bounded canvas workspaces — whiteboards, diagramming, Figma/Miro-like editing surfaces.
AI or rule-based chat bot screens with a prompt input and conversational reply bubbles.
Command palette or quick-action picker overlay (Cmd+K) with search and keyboard-driven actions.
Dedicated date-and-time picking screens or clock/time-zone utilities.
Map-centric screens showing a map as primary content with pins, routes, search, or location picking.
Photo or video editor screens with filters, crop, adjustments, trimming, or layered edits.
Screens that display or scan a QR code, often with a scanner viewfinder or a generated QR code image.
Chronological history or activity log screens (audit log, version history, browsing history, timeline view).
Timer, stopwatch, or clock screens with large time display and start/stop controls.
Video playback screens with video frame, scrubber, play/pause, volume, fullscreen, and captions.
Screens specifically captured in dark mode to illustrate the dark theme of any surface.
Admin panels, internal dashboards, back-office tools, or developer tools not shown to end users.
Anything that doesn't fit another Screen category — use sparingly as a fallback.
Column-based board layout (To Do / Doing / Done) with draggable cards, like Trello or Jira boards.
Layouts with two or more primary columns — dual-pane inbox, three-column Slack, master-detail-side layouts.
Collapsible section with a header that expands or collapses a content area when tapped, often with a chevron.
Horizontal trail of clickable path segments separated by '>' or '/' showing hierarchy and the current page.
Tappable action control with text and/or icon — primary, secondary, tertiary, or destructive filled/outlined buttons.
A small square that can be checked or unchecked to toggle a boolean option, often used in lists.
Control for picking a color — swatches, color wheel, sliders, or hex input.
Text field combined with a dropdown list of suggestions or selectable options (typeahead).
Control for selecting a date — calendar grid, wheel picker, or date input.
Inline-editable text that becomes a text field when clicked — commonly seen for renaming titles in place.
Control for uploading files — drag-and-drop zone, file chooser button, or upload area with file previews.
Circular button that floats above content in a fixed screen position, usually a '+' for a primary action.
Inline text link (typically underlined or colored) that navigates elsewhere when clicked.
Row of small dots indicating current page/position in a carousel or paginated content (dot indicators).
Numbered page navigation control with Previous/Next and page numbers (e.g., < 1 2 3 >).
Circular selector in a group where only one option can be selected at a time.
Star rating, thumbs-up/down, or emoji rating control used to capture a rating from the user.
Text input with a magnifying-glass icon for searching, often with a clear button and placeholder like 'Search'.
Pill-shaped row of 2+ mutually exclusive options where one is highlighted as selected (like iOS segmented control).
Dropdown select control showing a single value with a caret that opens a list of options.
Horizontal track with a draggable thumb used to pick a value within a range.
+/- control for incrementing or decrementing a numeric value in small steps.
Toggle control (iOS-style switch) that flips a setting on or off, often with a colored background when on.
Horizontal row of tab labels where selecting one swaps the content area below it.
Single- or multi-line text input box for user-entered text, with a label, placeholder, or helper text.
Tappable rectangular block (larger than a chip, simpler than a card) used to present options in a grid.
Control for selecting a time of day — clock face, wheel picker, or hour/minute inputs.
Small label or dot attached to an element showing a count or status (red notification dot, '99+' bubble).
Wide, full-width attention bar across a screen — announcements, alerts, or promotional banners.
Contained rectangular unit (usually with a shadow or border) grouping related content like an image, title, and actions.
Horizontally scrollable or swipeable row of cards/images, often paired with page dots.
Small, pill-shaped element representing a tag, filter, selected option, or person (with optional close icon).
Thin horizontal or vertical line used to separate groups of content.
Grid or mosaic of images — photo gallery, media library thumbnails.
A list presented in a grid of tiles or cards (as opposed to a vertical list).
Visual representation of a keyboard key or shortcut, like 'Cmd + K' badges in UI.
Spinner or circular progress indicator showing that content is loading (indeterminate).
Marker or pin icon placed on a map to indicate a location.
Determinate progress bar or circular progress showing percent complete, step count, or upload progress.
Vertical navigation rail or sidebar down the left (or right) side of a screen with nav items and icons.
Gray placeholder shapes mimicking the layout of loading content (skeleton screens).
Vertical list of rows stacked top-to-bottom — list items, settings rows, inbox rows.
Small colored dot indicating online/offline, live, or status (green/yellow/red dot).
Data table with rows and columns, column headers, and optionally sortable/filterable cells.
Outline or jump-to-section list indicating the structure of a long document or page.
Compact bar of action icons/buttons, often at the top or bottom of a view (formatting toolbar, editor toolbar).
Horizontal bar at the top of a screen with title, back button, and action icons (app bar, nav bar, header).
Hierarchical tree view with expandable/collapsible parent-child nodes (file tree, org chart).
Tooltip-style annotations layered over the UI to explain elements during onboarding, often numbered.
Right-click or long-press menu that appears next to an item with contextual actions.
Modal dialog box centered over content with a title, body, and action buttons (OK/Cancel).
Panel that slides in from an edge of the screen (left, right, top, or bottom) — side drawer or bottom sheet.
Menu that opens below a button or trigger with a list of selectable actions or options.
A full-screen modal overlay that takes over the entire viewport, often used for lightboxes or takeovers.
Expanded navigation overlay (often the hamburger menu) that takes over part or all of the screen.
Small overlay anchored to a trigger element, floating over content with arrow/tail pointing to its source.
Short, auto-dismissing notification appearing briefly at the top or bottom of the screen (snackbar).
Small hover/long-press hint showing a brief text label about an element.
Circular (or squircle) profile image representing a person, account, or group — may show initials if no photo.
Small, single-concept pictogram used in buttons, lists, and navigation (usually monochromatic line or filled icon).
Decorative, flat or stylized illustration — often used in empty states, onboarding, and marketing surfaces.
Brand logo or wordmark for an app, product, or company.
Photographic image — real-world photography as opposed to illustration or icon.
Animated content or video playing inline — Lottie animations, looping videos, GIFs embedded in the UI.
Large, prominent image/graphic at the top of a screen used as a banner or header (hero/banner image).
Small preview image representing a larger asset (video thumb, file preview, album art thumbnail).
